chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The resident should not lead the traveler in prayer, nor should the traveler lead the resident. If one is tested by one of these situations (i.e., leading the other), and the traveler leads a group of residents, he should complete two rak'ahs, then say the taslim (salutation), then take the hand of one of them and place him in front to lead them. And if the traveler prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as two rak'ahs, then say the taslim. And if he prays with them for Dhuhr, he should consider the first two as Dhuhr and the last two as Asr.
And from him (Sa'd), from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu al-Mi'ya Humayd ibn al-Muthanna, from Imran, from Muhammad ibn Ali:

He asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is traveling when he joins the prayer with those who are resident. He said: 'He should complete his prayer (as two rak'ahs), then say the taslim, and consider the last two (rak'ahs) as a single unit of lightness (subhah).'.

key_terms.سُبْحَةً: A light/short prayer or unit of voluntary prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a traveler leading residents in prayer or praying behind them according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential hierarchy in congregational prayer, prioritizing the resident (muqim) over the traveler (musafir) to maintain order, while providing practical solutions for when this hierarchy is inverted. It details the specific procedural adjustments for both scenarios, such as the traveler leading residents completing only two rak'ahs and appointing a resident to finish, or the traveler praying behind residents and treating the additional time as voluntary (suhbah). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the integrity of the obligatory prayer structure while accommodating the concessions granted to travelers.
